### Environmental Planning and Historic Preservation Decision Support System
#### USCG-2024-0704, Safety Zone; Empire Wind 1 Wind Farm Project Area, Outer Continental Shelf, Lease OCS-A 0512, Offshore New York and New Jersey, Atlantic Ocean - Project Approved Status
###### • In Preparation (08/21/2024) • Environmental Review (08/29/2024) • Senior Environmental Review (08/30/2024) • Proponent Review (09/04/2024) • Project Approved (09/04/2024)
#### Project Information
###### General Name: USCG-2024-0704, Safety Zone; Empire Wind 1 Wind Farm Project Area, Outer Continental Shelf, Lease OCS-A 0512, Offshore New York and New Jersey, Atlantic Ocean DSS ID: DSS-USCG-2024-20428 Security: Unclassified Description: The Coast Guard proposes to establish 55 temporary safety zones around the construction of each facility during the development of the Empire Wind 1 Wind Farm project area within federal waters on the Outer Continental Shelf, specifically in the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management Renewable Energy Lease Area OCS-A 0512, approximately 12 nautical miles south of Long Island, NY. This action protects life, property, and the environment during construction of each facility from March 1, 2025, to February 29, 2028. When enforced, only attending vessels and vessels with authorization are permitted to enter or remain in the temporary safety zones. ###### • Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ): Empire Wind 1 Wind Farm project area within federal waters on the OCS. Specifically, the BOEM Renewable Energy Lease Area OCS-A 0512, approximately 12 NM offshore south of Long Island, NY, and 17 NM offshore east of Long Branch, NJ.

#### Comments

###### • • •

###### Madeleine McNamara (Level I), Environmental sensitivity determination of no effect for the on- water activity associated with the temporary safety zones on the outer continental shelf, 12nm south of Long Island, in the vicinity of position 40° 20' 25.307"N 73° 26' 50.160"W. No effect determination based on the following natural resource agency mapping tools: USFWS Information for Planning and Consultation (IPaC), NOAA Environmental Response Management Application (ERMA), NOAA Essential Fish Habitat Mapper (EFH), NOAA Environmental Sensitivity Index (ESI), NOAA National Endangered Species Act (ESA) Critical Habitat Mapper, various state mapping tools for eelgrass, and the mapping tool for land areas of Federally-Recognized Tribes by the Bureau of Indian Affairs. See attached safety zone environmental sensitivity table and USFWS species list. (08/30/2024 12:39:13) Madeleine McNamara (Level I), The on-water activity associated with the temporary safety zones on the outer continental shelf, 12nm south of Long Island, will have no effect to the Roseate Tern or migratory birds. Sturgeon, critical fish habitat, shellfish/invertebrates, eelgrass, and wetlands are not present in the area. Sea turtles, whales, winter flounder, and diadromous fish may be present in the area but will not be impacted by the safety zone which will limit access to the area. (08/30/2024 12:38:23) Madeleine McNamara (Level I), The temporary safety zones on the outer continental shelf, 12nm south of Long Island, will have no effect on public health or safety with regards to environmental justice considerations; air quality; noise impacts; hazardous wastes and/or contamination; wastewater; potable water; or changes in modes or safety of transportation. The proposed safety zones do not employ new or unproven technology that is likely to involve unique or unknown environmental risks, where the effect on the human environment is likely to be highly uncertain, or where the effect on the human environment is likely to be highly controversial in terms of scientific validity. The on-water activity associated with establishing the safety zone has no intersection to Section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act. (08/30/2024 12:36:11)
